questions.prompt: Use the order-reversal property to rewrite \(\int_4^1 x^2\,dx\) with lower limit \(1\) and upper limit \(4\).
questions.answer:
Reversing the limits changes the sign:
\[\int_4^1 x^2\,dx=-\int_1^4 x^2\,dx.\]

Changing the order of the bounds multiplies the integral by \(-1\). Therefore
\[\int_6^1 f(x)\,dx=-\int_1^6 f(x)\,dx=-9.\]

An antiderivative of \(x\) is \(x^2/2\).
\[\int_0^2 x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^2=\frac{4}{2}-0=2.\]

Integrate term by term:
\[\int(2x+1)\,dx=x^2+x.\]
Then evaluate at the bounds:
\[(3^2+3)-(1^2+1)=12-2=10.\]

Integrate each term:
\[\int(x^3-2x+5)\,dx=\frac{x^4}{4}-x^2+5x.\]
Evaluate:
\[\left(\frac{16}{4}-4+10\right)-\left(\frac14-1+5\right)=10-\frac{17}{4}=\frac{23}{4}.\]

An antiderivative of \(\sin x\) is \(-\cos x\).
\[\int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx=[-\cos x]_0^\pi=-\cos\pi-(-\cos0).\]
Since \(\cos\pi=-1\) and \(\cos0=1\), the value is \(1+1=2\).

questions.prompt: The velocity of a particle is \(v(t)=6t-2\) metres per second. Find its displacement from \(t=1\) to \(t=4\).
questions.answer:
Displacement is the signed integral of velocity:
\[\int_1^4(6t-2)\,dt=[3t^2-2t]_1^4.\]
At \(4\): \(48-8=40\). At \(1\): \(3-2=1\).
So the displacement is \(40-1=39\) m.

questions.prompt: Find the signed area \(\int_{-2}^{2} x^3\,dx\), and explain why the value is reasonable.
questions.answer:
An antiderivative is \(x^4/4\).
\[\int_{-2}^{2}x^3\,dx=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\frac{16}{4}-\frac{16}{4}=0.\]
This is reasonable because \(x^3\) is odd: the negative signed area on \([-2,0]\) cancels the positive signed area on \([0,2]\).

questions.prompt: Find the area between \(y=x+2\) and the \(x\)-axis from \(x=-1\) to \(x=3\).
Find the area between \(y=4-x^2\) and the \(x\)-axis from \(x=-2\) to \(x=2\).

questions.answer:
Take \(k\) outside the integral:
\[\int_0^2kx\,dx=k\int_0^2x\,dx=k\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^2=2k.\]
Set \(2k=12\), so \(k=6\).

Evaluate in terms of \(a\):
\[\int_0^a3x^2\,dx=[x^3]_0^a=a^3.\]
So \(a^3=24\). Because \(a>0\),
\[a=\sqrt[3]{24}=2\sqrt[3]{3}.\]

Compute the integral:
\[\int_{-c}^{c}(x^2-1)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-x\right]_{-c}^{c}.\]
This equals \((c^3/3-c)-(-c^3/3+c)=2c^3/3-2c\).
Set it to zero:
\[\frac{2c^3}{3}-2c=2c\left(\frac{c^2}{3}-1\right)=0.\]
Thus \(c=0\) or \(c^2=3\), so \(c=0,\pm\sqrt3\).

questions.prompt: A student says \(\int_{-1}^{1} x^2\,dx=0\) because the limits are symmetric. Identify the error and find the correct value.
questions.answer:
Symmetric limits only force cancellation for odd functions. The function \(x^2\) is even and non-negative, so the areas add.
\[\int_{-1}^{1}x^2\,dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{1}=\frac13-\left(-\frac13\right)=\frac23.\]

questions.prompt: Find the total area between \(y=x\) and the \(x\)-axis from \(x=-2\) to \(x=3\).
questions.answer:
Total area uses absolute value because \(x\) is below the axis on \([-2,0]\) and above it on \([0,3]\).
\[\text{Area}=\int_{-2}^{0}(-x)\,dx+\int_0^3x\,dx.\]
\[\int_{-2}^{0}(-x)\,dx=\left[-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-2}^{0}=2,\quad \int_0^3x\,dx=\frac92.\]
Total area \(=2+9/2=13/2\).

questions.prompt: Suppose \(f(x)\ge0\) on \([0,2]\), \(f(x)\le0\) on \([2,5]\), \(\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx=7\), and \(\int_2^5 f(x)\,dx=-4\). Find the signed area and the total area from \(0\) to \(5\).
questions.answer:
The signed area is the definite integral over the whole interval:
\[\int_0^5 f(x)\,dx=\int_0^2f(x)\,dx+\int_2^5f(x)\,dx=7+(-4)=3.\]
The total area treats the below-axis part as positive. Since \(f\le0\) on \([2,5]\), that area is \(4\).
Total area \(=7+4=11\).
